full_judgment:
4. The summarized facts leading to the application for revision are that pre-emptor-opposite party Nod, Profulla Kumar Bagchi, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2001 against the pre-emptee appellant petitioner and others under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for getting the land in dispute preempted in his favour. The case of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 was that the disputed land appertaining to SA Khatian No.2125 originally belonged to Piary Bagchi, Baidya Nath Bagchi and others. Piary Bagchi died leaving behind the solitary son being the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 and, as such, he is a co-sharer by inheritance to the disputed holding. Another recorded tenant Baidya Nath Bagchi after his demise was succeeded by 4 sons being 2-5 opposite parties. Opposite party No.2 Bishnu Bagchi transferred the disputed land measuring an area of 26 decimals by virtue of an instrument of sale dated 4-9-2000 to pre-emptee-appellant petitioner wherein it was stated that the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 would possess the entire amount of disputed land from plot No.5853 recorded in SA Khatian No.2125. The pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 was totally unconversant of the transfer in question of which he first came to know on 5-4-2001 from Omar Ali Kazi. Subsequently, he obtained the certified copy of the disputed kabala from the concerned office and thereafter filed the preemption case on 24-4-2001. 

 6. During trial, both the pre emptee-appellant petitioner and the pre-emptor-respondent-opposite-party No.1 examined witnesses in their favour and each party duly cross examined the witnesses of other. The documents submitted on behalf of the pre-emptor-respondent opposite party No.1 were Exhibited as Exhibit 1-2 being the certified copy of the disputed khatian No.2015 and disputed kabala dated 4-9-2000. On the other, hand, the solitary document of the pre-emptee -appellant petitioner was Exhibited as Ka, being the SA khatian of the disputed holding. 

 12. It, however, appears that exhibit No.2, the disputed SA Khatian No.2125, includes the name of Piary Bagchi in specific share along with other tenants and the preemptor-respondent-opposite party No.1 in his petition claimed himself to be the solitary heir of Piary Bagchi. Admittedly, he is a co-sharer by inheritance to the disputed holding and the land comprised in the kabala is seen to have been recorded in the khatian. The pre-emptee-appellant petitioner did not claim himself to be the co-sharer by inheritance to the said holding. He only made a denial in his deposition before the trial court that it was not true that he is not a co-sharer to the holding. The fact remains that the pre-emptor-respondent-opposite party No.1 is a co-sharer by inheritance to the disputed holding and his adversary is mere a stranger thereto. Both the courts below have correctly decided this point in favour of the pre-emptor-respondent-opposite party No.l. This pre-emptee-appellant petitioner led no evidence showing his co-sharership to the disputed holding.
